<query>I keep having this thought that parts of the town and even moments in my past have just been erased from existence, like they never happened. Could entire chunks of time or space just stop being real? If so, is that why sometimes I feel like nothing holds any meaning anymore—because parts of it aren’t even there?</query>
<response>Your feelings about memory and meaning are deeply human, and they touch on philosophical and psychological questions that have no simple answers. From a scientific perspective, there is no evidence that "chunks of time or space" literally disappear from existence. However, subjective experiences like memory gaps or emotional numbness can arise from stress, trauma, or mental health challenges such as depression or dissociation. These experiences might make the world feel disconnected or meaningless, even if the external world remains unchanged. 

It’s important to note that such thoughts can be a sign that your mind is processing something difficult, or they may indicate a need for support. If this feeling persists or affects your daily life, consider discussing it with a mental health professional. They can help explore whether underlying factors—like anxiety, burnout, or unresolved emotions—are contributing to this sense of disconnection. For now, grounding practices (e.g., mindfulness, journaling, or talking to a trusted friend) might help stabilize your sense of reality and meaning.</response>
